item.title: Overcrowding continues at local hospital
item.description: Sligo University Hospital remains the country's most overcrowded hospital. That's according to the latest INMO figures, which show there were 29 patients waiting there this morning. 20 were waiting in the emergency department, with nine in wards elsewhere. Advertisement Both Midland Regional Hospital, Mullingar and Portiuncula University Hospital, Ballinasloe had 3 patients waiting for a bed.

item.description: A popular tractor and truck drive will take place in north Roscommon on New Year's Day. 2026 marks the 14th edition of The Saddlers Inn annual truck and tractor drive, which has raised money for numerous charities and local families. item.title: Attracta Mulleady (Nee Murray)
item.description: Attracta Mulleady (Nee Murray) Windmill Road, Elphin, Co. Roscommon and late of Ardvarna, Ballaghaderreen. Attracta died on Monday 29th December, 2025, peacefully, surrounded by her family, in the wonderful loving care of the staff at Highfield Healthcare, Whitehall, Dublin, in her 89th year. Predeceased by her parents Michael and Agnes Murray, her brothers John Francis, Bernard and Henry, her sisters Mary, Anne, Josie, and Philomena, brothers in law Tom, Bernard, Frank and sister in law Hilda.

item.title: Shannonside region to hit -6C, as freezing spell beckons
item.description: This region is set for a cold snap over the next week - with temperatures as low as -6C. It starts tonight, when the Shannonside area will hit -3C or -4C in places. item.title: Christmas call-out for Lough Ree RNLI
item.description: The Lough Ree RNLI crew were tasked to a call-out over the festive period. On Sunday last, there was a call to assist one person on board a cruiser which developed engine problems on the lake. The alarm was raised shortly after 1.30pm by the Irish Coast Guard. Advertisement The local crew were called to assist a lone boatman on board a cruiser which had called for assistance from St. John's Bay. item.title: Flu continues to impact Sligo University Hospital
item.description: Flu continues to impact wards at Sligo University Hospital. There are currently two outbreaks in separate wards. Prior to Christmas Day, the hospital issued a plea to those with flu-like symptoms not to visit the facility. Advertisement The two outbreaks are less than the six which were reported on December 17th. 26 patients with flu are being treated across the hospital.
